questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Aluminium upon reaction with NaOH forms $[Al(OH)_6]^{3-}$ ion.
Statement II: The geometry of $ICl_4^-$, $ClO_3^-$ and $IBr_2^-$ is square planar, pyramidal and linear respectively.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Statement I:
Aluminium reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide to form sodium tetrahydroxoaluminate(III) and liberates hydrogen gas. The reaction is given by:
$2Al + 2NaOH + 6H_2O \rightarrow 2Na^+[Al(OH)_4]^- + 3H_2$
The complex ion formed is $[Al(OH)_4]^-$, not $[Al(OH)_6]^{3-}$. Thus, Statement I is false.

Statement II:
For $ICl_4^-$, the central iodine atom has $7$ valence electrons $+ 1$ (from negative charge) $= 8$ electrons. It forms $4$ sigma bonds with Cl atoms and has $2$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square planar.
For $ClO_3^-$, the central chlorine atom has $7$ valence electrons $+ 1 = 8$ electrons. It forms $3$ sigma bonds with O atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is trigonal pyramidal.
For $IBr_2^-$, the central iodine atom has $7$ valence electrons $+ 1 = 8$ electrons. It forms $2$ sigma bonds with Br atoms and has $3$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3d$ and the shape is linear.
Thus, Statement II is true.

Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.q:
Consider the following reactions
$\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{~B}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{7} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2 \mathrm{X}+$\mathrm{Y}$
$\mathrm{CuSO}_{4}+$\mathrm{Y}$ \xrightarrow{$\text{ Non-Luminous flame }$} $\mathrm{Z}+$\mathrm{SO}_{3}$
$2 $\mathrm{Z}+$2 $\mathrm{X}+$ Carbon $\xrightarrow{$\text{ Luminous flame }$} 2 $\mathrm{Q}+\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{~B}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{7}+$\mathrm{CO}$
The oxidation states of Cu in Z and Q, respectively are :
questions.solution:
The given reactions describe the Borax Bead Test.
When borax ($Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O$) is heated, it first loses water and then melts to form a transparent glassy bead consisting of sodium metaborate ($NaBO_2$) and boric anhydride ($B_2O_3$).
$Na_2B_4O_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2NaBO_2 (X) + B_2O_3 (Y)$
In the non-luminous (oxidizing) flame, $B_2O_3$ reacts with $CuSO_4$ to form copper(II) metaborate ($Z$), which is blue in color.
$CuSO_4 + B_2O_3 \xrightarrow{Non-Luminous} Cu(BO_2)_2 (Z) + SO_3$
In $Cu(BO_2)_2$, the oxidation state of $Cu$ is $+2$.
In the luminous (reducing) flame, the copper(II) metaborate is reduced by carbon to copper(I) metaborate ($Q$), which is colorless/red.
$2Cu(BO_2)_2 (Z) + 2NaBO_2 (X) + C \xrightarrow{Luminous} 2CuBO_2 (Q) + Na_2B_4O_7 + CO$
In $CuBO_2$, the oxidation state of $Cu$ is $+1$.
Therefore, the oxidation states of $Cu$ in $Z$ and $Q$ are $+2$ and $+1$ respectively.

questions.q:
It is noticed that $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}$ but $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$ is less stable than $\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$. Observe the following reactions.
$\mathrm{PbO}_{2}+\mathrm{Pb} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{PbO} ; \Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{G}^{\circ}(1)$
$\mathrm{SnO}_{2}+\mathrm{Sn} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{SnO} ; \Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{G}^{\circ}(2)$
Identify the correct set from the following
questions.solution:
The stability of oxidation states in Group 14 is governed by the inert pair effect, which increases down the group.
For Lead ($Pb$), the $+2$ oxidation state is more stable than the $+4$ state ($Pb^{2+} > Pb^{4+}$).
In the reaction $PbO_2 + Pb \rightarrow 2PbO$, $Pb^{4+}$ is being reduced to $Pb^{2+}$ and $Pb^0$ is being oxidized to $Pb^{2+}$. Since the product contains the more stable oxidation state, the reaction is spontaneous, meaning $\Delta_r G^\circ(1) < 0$.
For Tin ($Sn$), the $+4$ oxidation state is more stable than the $+2$ state ($Sn^{4+} > Sn^{2+}$).
In the reaction $SnO_2 + Sn \rightarrow 2SnO$, the stable $Sn^{4+}$ is being converted into the less stable $Sn^{2+}$. This process is non-spontaneous, meaning $\Delta_r G^\circ(2) > 0$.
Thus, the correct set is $\Delta_r G^\circ(1) < 0$ and $\Delta_r G^\circ(2) > 0$.

questions.q:
The correct statements from the following are :
A. Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decreases down the group.
B. Electronegativity of group 13 elements decreases down the group.
C. Among the group 13 elements, Boron has highest first ionisation enthalpy.
D. The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Analyzing statements about Group 13 elements (B, Al, Ga, In, Tl):
A. Ionic radii of M³⁺ cations: Down a group, more electron shells are added, so ionic radii increase, not decrease. FALSE
B. Electronegativity: Generally decreases down the group, though Ga shows an anomaly with higher electronegativity than Al. The statement is approximately true but has exceptions.
C. First ionization enthalpy: B (800.6 kJ/mol) is highest due to smallest size and highest nuclear charge density. Al (577.5), Ga (579), In (558), Tl (589). TRUE
D. Trichlorides and triodides: BCl₃, AlCl₃, GaCl₃, etc. are all covalent compounds (electron-deficient). BI₃, AlI₃, GaI₃, etc. are also covalent (I⁻ is large and polarizable). TRUE
The clearly correct statements are C and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Elements ' $X$ ' and ' $Y$ ' are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively among $\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{As}, \mathrm{Sb}$ and P. The nature of the oxides $\mathrm{X}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{Y}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ is acidic and amphoteric, respectively.
Statement II : $\quad \mathrm{BCl}_{3}$ is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water. It produces $\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}\right]^{-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{B}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ in aqueous medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
For Statement I:
Among N, As, Sb, P, the electronegativity order is N > P > As > Sb. Thus X = N (most electronegative) and Y = Sb (least electronegative). $N_2O_3$ is acidic (forms HNO₂ with water) and $Sb_2O_3$ is amphoteric (reacts with both acids and bases).
Statement I is true.
For Statement II:
While $BCl_3$ is covalent and hydrolyzes in water to form $B(OH)_3$, the hydrolysis products are incorrect. In neutral aqueous medium, $B(OH)_3$ is formed. The tetrahedral $[B(OH)_4]^-$ forms only in basic conditions, and boron does not form $[B(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ (boron is not a typical transition metal).
Statement II is false.

Thus, acidic nature is in order ${BF}_{3} < {BCl}_{3} < {BBr}_{3} < {Bl}_{3}$.
